title: Activity Lifecycle
objectives: Save and restore state across config changes
Avoid leaks and lost work on rotation

sections.markdown: The activity lifecycle is the ordered set of callbacks Android invokes as an Activity is created, shown, hidden and destroyed, letting you set up and release resources at the right time.

sections.code:
onCreate -> onStart -> onResume   (now visible & interactive)
   ... user leaves ...
onPause -> onStop -> onDestroy
   ... return ...
onRestart -> onStart -> onResume

sections.markdown: Doing heavy work in onPause — it blocks the next activity from showing. Keep onPause fast; persist heavy data in onStop. Also: a rotation destroys and recreates the activity, losing in-memory state.
Survive config changes with a ViewModel (kept across recreation) for UI state, and onSaveInstanceState for small bundles. ViewModel is the modern answer.

flashcards.back: The activity is destroyed and recreated; in-memory state is lost unless saved (ViewModel / onSaveInstanceState).
It runs before the next activity becomes visible, so slow work delays the UI.

quiz.q: Which callback makes an activity interactive?
quiz.explain: onResume is the last step before the user can interact.
Configuration changes recreate the activity unless handled.

quiz.q: Best place to persist important data?
quiz.explain: onStop is a safe point to persist data before the activity is no longer visible.

challenges.text: Log every lifecycle callback and rotate to observe the sequence.
Preserve a form's text across rotation using onSaveInstanceState.
Move UI state into a ViewModel and survive config changes cleanly.
Diagnose and fix an activity leak caused by a long-lived callback/handler.
